VMj-3S1tku0.summary: Andrej Karpathy's first Neural Networks: Zero to Hero lecture, which builds micrograd, a tiny autograd engine, from scratch in Python. It explains backpropagation and neural network training step by step, assuming only basic Python and some high-school calculus.
VMj-3S1tku0.why: HN treats it as the best starting point for really understanding backprop and neural nets, because Karpathy explains the why with intuition and builds everything in code.

VscdPA6sUkc.summary: David Brevik's GDC 2016 postmortem of Diablo covers how it went from a turn-based claymation DOS concept to a real-time action RPG, plus the story of Blizzard North and development anecdotes.
VscdPA6sUkc.why: Frequently recommended whenever Diablo or its origins come up, for its candid account of the human side of game development.

VZQoAKJPbh8.summary: Chris Granger, creator of Light Table and the Eve language, gives a Berkeley data science lecture on what computation and programming might look like in ten years. He covers the path that led to Eve and ends with demos.
VZQoAKJPbh8.why: HN keeps pointing to it as a thoughtful vision of programming for non-programmers and as background on Eve's motivations.

VUhlNx_-wYk.summary: Tom Stuart's Ruby Manor 3 talk builds FizzBuzz using nothing but Ruby lambdas, working through Church encodings of numbers, booleans and data structures. It is a hands-on introduction to lambda calculus.
VUhlNx_-wYk.why: Strongly recommended in lambda calculus and Y-combinator threads as a mind-expanding half hour that clarifies the ideas.

VAhHkJQ3KgY.summary: A /noclip interview with Tarn Adams of Bay 12 Games about Dwarf Fortress: where the ASCII simulation came from, how it works, and the plans for its Steam release. It includes his telling of the famous bug in which cats were poisoned by alcohol.
VAhHkJQ3KgY.why: HN points to it whenever Dwarf Fortress comes up, mainly for the alcohol-poisoned cats bug story and a developer's view of the game's depth.

VQKMoT-6XSg.summary: The full 80-minute Macworld 2007 keynote in which Steve Jobs introduced the original iPhone. It includes the multitouch demos, visual voicemail and scrolling.
VQKMoT-6XSg.why: Cited as a landmark tech presentation, especially for the audience's astonished reaction to touch scrolling and demo moments like visual voicemail.

VO6XEQIsCoM.summary: Psychologist Barry Schwartz argues in this TED talk that abundant choice makes people more paralyzed and dissatisfied rather than freer and happier.
VO6XEQIsCoM.why: HN recommends it as the standard talk on how too many options lead to paralysis and second-guessing.

Vjm8P8utT5g.summary: A tool-assisted speedrun of Pokemon Yellow by MrWint that uses arbitrary code execution to push Game Boy hardware to its limits. Through crafted inputs it injects code and ends up running other programs, such as Tetris, inside the game.
Vjm8P8utT5g.why: HN points to it as the standard demonstration of arbitrary code execution on a Game Boy, and of glitches and bugs being turned into a working computer.

V4V2bpZlqx8.summary: Numberphile's Dr James Grime explains the flaw in the Enigma machine, namely that a letter could never be encrypted to itself, and how that helped the Allies break the code. It touches on the Bombe and Alan Turing.
V4V2bpZlqx8.why: HN points to it as a short, clear explanation of why Enigma was breakable and how search-space elimination works.

VBwWbFpkltg.summary: David Heinemeier Hansson's opening keynote at RailsConf 2019 argues against the expectation of payment for open source work, drawing on his experience releasing Rails. It also includes lighter asides about the industry.
VBwWbFpkltg.why: It is the go-to reference in debates about whether open source maintainers are owed compensation, and commenters say it is worth watching even for non-Rails developers.

VDfX44fZoMc.summary: J. B. Rainsberger argues that large integrated tests are a scam: they are slow, fail opaquely, and give a false sense of coverage. He advocates focused collaboration and contract tests at boundaries instead.
VDfX44fZoMc.why: HN recommends it in testing-strategy debates as the classic case for fewer integration tests and more small, well-contracted unit tests.

VNvzZfsC13o.summary: Real Engineering analyzes whether electric planes are feasible, focusing on battery energy density limits compared with jet fuel. It concludes electric flight works mainly for short ranges.
VNvzZfsC13o.why: HN recommends it as a clear explanation of why batteries limit electric aviation.

VO_1AdYRGW8.summary: A neural-network upscaled 4K, 60 fps version of the 1906 film of a trip down Market Street in San Francisco, shot four days before the earthquake. It shows cable cars, horse carriages, early automobiles and pedestrians sharing the street.
VO_1AdYRGW8.why: Cited in threads on cars, streets and urbanism as evidence of how mixed traffic worked before cars took over.

VPBH1eW28mo.summary: A five-minute CGP Grey explainer arguing that a phone is effectively an extension of your mind, and that any backdoor or master key into encrypted devices will inevitably be abused or leaked. It frames the encryption debate as locks that are either unbreakable or absent.
VPBH1eW28mo.why: HN commenters use it as a short, persuasive primer to send to non-technical people in debates over encryption backdoors and decryption legislation.

VeAdryYZ7ak.summary: Peter Seibel's 2006 Google TechTalk on Practical Common Lisp, framed by the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis and Paul Graham's Blub paradox. It shows Lisp features such as condition restarts and its generic-function object system.
VeAdryYZ7ak.why: HN remembers it as the memorable explanation of restarts and multiple dispatch, referenced whenever those features come up.

VESMU7JfVHU.summary: A short film made with cold neutron imaging at the Paul Scherrer Institut showing a moka pot brewing coffee, sped up four times. The neutron beam makes the water and steam inside the pot visible.
VESMU7JfVHU.why: Recommended in moka pot threads as the best way to see how the pot works from the inside.

VFFlO7yBIBM.summary: Unreleased 1996 footage of the Wired editors interviewing Bill Gates when he visited their office. Gates talks about software, the internet and Microsoft's thinking at the time. The video is about 53 minutes long.
VFFlO7yBIBM.why: People recommend it as a rare, unpolished look at Gates's mid-90s thinking, including predictions that aged well and badly.

Vj04MKykmnQ.summary: Naomi Wu visits the Shenzhen offices of smartphone maker UMIDIGI in person to get them to release source code they owed under the GPLv2, and they comply.
Vj04MKykmnQ.why: Held up as a rare success story of GPL enforcement against a Chinese hardware company, and admired for the effort.

V2YDApNRK3g.summary: The Thought Emporium builds a homemade multi-electrode array, grows human neurons on it and attempts to take readings. It is the first part of a series aimed at connecting living neurons to a computer.
V2YDApNRK3g.why: HN cites it as an impressive garage-science example of neuron-computer interfaces and hard-science DIY biology.

VLxTHYGLKY0.summary: A Plogue developer shows the custom electronic test rigs built to measure the Sega Mega Drive/Genesis sound chip (YM2612) for the chipsynth MD emulation. It covers the years of testing and reverse engineering needed to reproduce the chip's quirks accurately.
VLxTHYGLKY0.why: Recommended in threads on chip emulation as a look at how hard it is to emulate vintage sound hardware accurately.

VVp8UGjECt4.summary: Economist-comedian Yoram Bauman delivers a humorous translation of Mankiw's ten principles of economics for the uninitiated. It was presented at the AAAS humor session in 2007.
VVp8UGjECt4.why: HN points to it as a short, funny and genuinely informative take on economic principles such as trade and opportunity cost.

VYhAGnsnO7w.summary: Dave Jones of EEVblog looks at a sub-3-cent microcontroller from Padauk and other obscure Chinese manufacturers. He shows how to find such parts and where to buy them in stock.
VYhAGnsnO7w.why: Cited as the go-to demo that full microcontrollers now cost about three cents, replacing things like the 555 timer.

VjE0Kdfos4Y.summary: A short BBC clip in which David Attenborough shows a lyrebird imitating sounds, including camera shutters, car alarms and chainsaws. It comes from the BBC natural history series Life on Earth.
VjE0Kdfos4Y.why: Brought up whenever threads touch on mimicry, voice cloning or bird vocalization, and people say the ending is startling.

VkIJbpdTujE.summary: A Computerphile video in which Dr Mike Pound and PhD student Lewis Stuart explain 3D Gaussian splatting, a quick technique that turns photos of a scene into a 3D model without much compute. It includes a demo and compares the approach to NeRFs.
VkIJbpdTujE.why: HN recommends it as an accessible introduction to Gaussian splats, made by people who understand the subject.

V6VP-2aIcSc.summary: Brian Will critiques object-oriented programming and rewrites a roughly 3800-line OO program in a procedural style, cutting code and complexity. It is part of a series of OOP critiques.
V6VP-2aIcSc.why: HN recommends it as a concrete, worked example of the case against heavy OOP rather than abstract argument.

VHWUCX6osgM.summary: Steve Jobs's 2005 Stanford commencement address, in which he tells three stories about connecting the dots, love and loss, and death, including his remarks on typography.
VHWUCX6osgM.why: HN people recommend it as personal inspiration for perseverance and for keeping perspective by remembering mortality.

VPjODKUxV5g.summary: CityNerd critiques the Las Vegas Loop, the Boring Company's tunnel transit system, arguing its design and operation are poor. The video covers how the system actually runs.
VPjODKUxV5g.why: Used as the go-to critical, first-hand overview of the Vegas Loop in threads about the Boring Company.

VdqhHKjepiE.summary: RimWorld creator Tynan Sylvester explains at GDC 2017 how Ludeon framed the game as a story generator rather than a game. He covers the design methods that came out of that frame.
VdqhHKjepiE.why: Recommended as an accessible talk on emergent narrative and on how RimWorld was designed, and cited in threads on simulation games.

V2P8mjWRqpk.summary: Der8auer tours Hetzner's test lab and shows a custom AM5 server motherboard with the CPU socket rotated 90 degrees, built for rack airflow in their AX52 servers.
V2P8mjWRqpk.why: Pointed to as a look at Hetzner's unusual semi-custom server hardware and cooling.

V2aq5M3Q76U.summary: Matthew Garrett's linux.conf.au 2012 talk covers EFI and UEFI from the Linux point of view: why the PC BIOS was bad, what EFI changes, the issues it brings, and Secure Boot.
V2aq5M3Q76U.why: Pointed to as an entertaining, informative explanation of why UEFI is troublesome, from a Linux UEFI developer.

V8DfjXnIk6c.summary: Joe Rogan interviews ultramarathon runner Courtney Dauwalter shortly after she won the Moab 240 in under 58 hours. She tells stories of enduring extreme fatigue and hallucinations.
V8DfjXnIk6c.why: HN recommends it for her humility and for her stories of persevering through extreme endurance races.

V9K6gjR07Po.summary: Veritasium shows what the world looks like through a UV camera. It covers how pigments absorb UV, how fluorescence works, and how UV imaging reveals sunscreen effectiveness and skin damage.
V9K6gjR07Po.why: HN recommends it as a cool, eye-opening look at the hidden ultraviolet world, especially in sunscreen and vitamin D threads.

VI_riscmviI.summary: The first lesson of Martin Shkreli's introductory investing and finance course, running about two and a half hours. His related tutorials cover reading 10-K filings and building DCF models.
VI_riscmviI.why: HN mentions it with caveats: despite the author's reputation, commenters say it contains good investing and Excel material.

VNTQ-M_uSo8.summary: Stuart Halloway shows how Clojure's spec library lets you build programs that are both agile and robust. He covers declarative, predicate-based specification layered on interactive REPL development.
VNTQ-M_uSo8.why: Cited as an argument for runtime specs as an alternative to static typing, including a comparison of types, tests and spec.

VVV4xeWBIxE.summary: A Primitive Technology episode in which the creator builds a bow-drill-driven bark fan to blow air into a fire, using only natural materials. It shows the progression from fanning a fire by hand to a rotary forge blower.
VVV4xeWBIxE.why: HN readers like the channel for showing technology rebuilt from raw materials, and cite it as a vivid example of knowledge building on knowledge.

VdIURAu1-aU.summary: Geoff Hinton's 2010 Google Tech Talk on deep belief networks, learning layers of representation one at a time from unlabeled data, and extending them with multiplicative interactions.
VdIURAu1-aU.why: Cited as a watchable early introduction to deep learning from its pioneer, and remembered as a mind-blowing moment in the field.

VhWGQCzAtl8.summary: Extra Credits explains from a game developer's perspective why AAA games have stayed at $60 despite inflation, and how that pressure drives DLC, microtransactions and loot boxes.
VhWGQCzAtl8.why: HN uses it as a short explanation of AAA pricing economics in discussions of microtransactions and game pricing.

VnbiVw_1FNs.summary: Flanders and Swann perform 'First and Second Law', a comic song about the laws of thermodynamics, from their 1964 stage show At the Drop of Another Hat. It sets the first and second laws to a deadpan call-and-response routine.
VnbiVw_1FNs.why: HN brings it up whenever thermodynamics or entropy comes up, as the classic comic explanation of the laws.

Vrq2akzdFq8.summary: Adam Savage's Tested spends a week with the Magic Leap One developer kit. They dig into the hardware, display technology, user experience and launch apps.
Vrq2akzdFq8.why: HN recommends it as an in-depth independent review that tempers expectations and adds technical detail beyond Magic Leap's own materials.

VxINoKFm-S4.summary: David Christiansen gives a Strange Loop 2018 introduction to dependent types, where one language serves for both compile-time and run-time code and programs unite with proofs. It draws on his book The Little Typer.
VxINoKFm-S4.why: Recommended as an approachable introduction to dependent types and a preview of what The Little Typer covers.

VVUeqxXwCA0.summary: Not Just Bikes contrasts traditional and suburban development in North America. It looks at the financials behind each pattern and argues that suburban development leaves cities unable to pay for their own infrastructure.
VVUeqxXwCA0.why: Cited in urban planning threads as an accessible explanation of why low-density suburbs cost more to maintain than they bring in.

VcVfceTsD0A.summary: Lex Fridman interviews MIT physicist Max Tegmark, co-founder of the Future of Life Institute, about the case for pausing giant AI experiments and the risks of advanced AI.
VcVfceTsD0A.why: Recommended in AI-risk threads as a way to understand the safety-advocate argument for halting development.

VdjYVF4a6iU.summary: Ben Krasnow shows the first image from his home-built scanning electron microscope, after months of work, and walks through how the parts operate together.
VdjYVF4a6iU.why: Used as an example of Applied Science pushing the limits of garage engineering, in DIY microscope threads.

V-1RhQ1uuQ4.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day examines how bad actors and bots use Twitter, drawing on the released Russian IRA dataset and interviews. It asks why interactions on the platform turn hostile.
V-1RhQ1uuQ4.why: Cited in discussions of platform manipulation and eroding institutional trust, though mentions are mostly passing references.

V-vFtiDYiIw.summary: DIY Perks shows how to modify devices that use older USB connectors so they charge and connect over USB Type-C. He solders in a USB-C connector board and works through cases such as dongle-dependent gadgets and a mouse receiver.
V-vFtiDYiIw.why: Commenters cite it as a well-made, practical example of USB-C conversion when they discuss hacking USB-C into devices.

V74AxCqOTvg.summary: In a six-minute TED talk, Derek Sivers uses footage of a dancing man at an outdoor festival to show how a movement starts. He argues the first follower is what turns a lone nut into a leader.
V74AxCqOTvg.why: Recommended as a short leadership talk that commenters have shown to many people.

VAesMQ6VtK8.summary: A New York Times video on how China's sheltered internet produced a new breed of apps, centering on WeChat's all-in-one model combining payments, social and services. It suggests American companies are now taking cues from Chinese tech.
VAesMQ6VtK8.why: HN cites it as a concise explanation of why WeChat's super-app model is so dominant and why people worry about copycats.

VCH7BWGpl5s.summary: Thunderf00t critiques a 60 Minutes segment in which Navy pilots describe UFO encounters, arguing the footage has mundane explanations and has been debunked.
VCH7BWGpl5s.why: Used by skeptics in UFO threads as a debunking of the Navy pilot videos.

VJ-p9qOhBv4.summary: A one-minute clip from a cat cafe in Japan where sleeping cats wake and look around just before an earthquake begins shaking the room.
VJ-p9qOhBv4.why: Commenters use it in earthquake threads as an anecdote that animals may sense tremors seconds before humans, and occasionally as a joke about cat alarms.

VLHJUfgxEO4.summary: Urs Hoelzle, Google's SVP of infrastructure, gives the 2012 Open Networking Summit keynote on how Google adopted OpenFlow and software-defined networking in its own networks. The slides are linked in the description.
VLHJUfgxEO4.why: Cited as a primary source for Google building its own switches and running OpenFlow in production.

VOMWzjrRiBg.summary: An animated short on limits to growth, covering oil formation, peak oil, energy, economic growth and resource depletion. Its central section deals with exponential growth, and the author notes some statistics are dated.
VOMWzjrRiBg.why: HN links it in threads about energy shocks and resource dependence as a quick, accessible overview of peak-oil arguments.

VVvnTByzTmA.summary: An excerpt of a C-SPAN interview in which Thomas Sowell argues that preferential admission policies produce mismatch, dropouts and resentment.
VVvnTByzTmA.why: HN cites it in threads on college admissions and affirmative action as Sowell's argument about unintended consequences.

VaMjhwFE1Zw.summary: A VICE documentary profiling Wim Hof, the Iceman, covering his feats of cold endurance, his breathing and meditation method, and scientific studies of his control over his autonomic and immune systems.
VaMjhwFE1Zw.why: HN mentions it as evidence that the Wim Hof method can be learned and as the documentary that led some to try breathing and cold exposure, while others dispute the claims.

VeSgaJt27PM.summary: A Computer History Museum interview in which John Markoff of the New York Times talks with Douglas Engelbart about his life and research. It covers the influences and struggles behind his work on the mouse, hypertext and collaborative computing, and his aim of helping humanity tackle complex problems.
VeSgaJt27PM.why: HN cites it for Engelbart's own account of his philosophy, in which computers augment human thinking instead of mimicking paper.

VkR2hnXR0SM.summary: A five-minute CG sci-fi short film by Danil Krivoruchko, based on Peter Watts's novel Blindsight. It follows a revived crew member recalling a first contact mission, and took four years to make with artists worldwide.
VkR2hnXR0SM.why: Shared as a fan-made teaser for Blindsight in threads about the novel or alien intelligence.

Vn2vdQZhs0w.summary: Linus Tech Tips tests a large batch of DisplayPort cables with a Total Phase cable tester, checking bandwidth and signal quality. Many cables did not meet their claimed specs.
Vn2vdQZhs0w.why: HN cites it as evidence that DisplayPort cable labeling is unreliable and that even major brands can fail, and for its explanation of version differences.

VnvGwFegbC8.summary: A Tom Scott guest video by Grady Hillhouse of Practical Engineering on the 1981 Hyatt Regency walkway collapse. A seemingly minor change to the support design led to catastrophic failure, which is why the case is taught as a lesson to check and double-check everything.
VnvGwFegbC8.why: HN cites it as the standard case study of how a small unchecked design change causes disaster, and of why engineering process and bureaucracy exist.

VoS7DsT1rdM.summary: Rob Pike opens GopherCon 2014 with a keynote on the design and evolution of Go. He covers where its ideas came from, including the origin of hello world.
VoS7DsT1rdM.why: Recommended as a walkthrough of how Go's design evolved and where its ideas originated.

VpiNDxssUL0.summary: A 11:29 complete speedrun of Quake on Nightmare difficulty by the Quake done Quick team, assembled from separately recorded runs refined since 1996.
VpiNDxssUL0.why: HN uses it as a showcase of extreme FPS movement skill, such as rocket and grenade jumping.

VplMHWSZf5c.summary: Scott Aaronson's Harvard CMSA talk traces what mathematical truths are knowable, from Godel and Turing to the Busy Beaver function. He covers recent work on Busy Beaver values.
VplMHWSZf5c.why: Pointed to in Busy Beaver threads as an accessible expert talk on the topic.

VrKW58MS12g.summary: Mark Rober sets up elaborate glitter-bomb traps to go after phone scammers, working his way up their chain of command, and ends with a scammer being arrested. He also points viewers to fraud-reporting resources and to scambaiter Jim Browning's investigation.
VrKW58MS12g.why: HN mentions it in robocall and scam threads as an entertaining look at how phone scams work and how vigilantes fight back.

VsHc91IhzdI.summary: A one-minute visualization of a simulated ant colony in which ants follow pheromone trails, with the source code on GitHub. It shows emergent behavior arising from simple rules.
VsHc91IhzdI.why: Linked in ant-simulation threads as a compact, open-source example of emergent behavior.

Vt4Dfa4fOEY.summary: 'Skwerl' is a short film by Brian and Karl made entirely in fake English, imitating how English sounds to people who don't speak it. It was made for Kino Sydney and shown on QI.
Vt4Dfa4fOEY.why: HN cites it as the best-known example of gibberish that mimics the sound of a language, in threads about fake languages and nonsense imitations.

Vy5Ky50eGJs.summary: A short MIT Aerospace Controls Lab demo from 2011 of a variable pitch quadrotor flying.
Vy5Ky50eGJs.why: Referenced in drone threads as a demonstration that variable pitch quadcopters fly well with little drift.

V48M5j-6zdE.summary: TED talk by biochemist Cynthia Kenyon on how a simple genetic mutation can double the lifespan of the worm C. elegans, and what that suggests about extending healthy human life.
V48M5j-6zdE.why: Listed among resources in longevity and anti-aging discussions as a key piece of lifespan research.

V4sbYy0WdGQ.summary: The tipping scene from Reservoir Dogs, in which Mr. Pink explains why he does not believe in tipping.
V4sbYy0WdGQ.why: Linked in tipping debates as the classic argument against tipping culture.

V6CLumsir34.summary: A KATU News re-edit from remastered 4K footage of the 1970 Oregon incident in which officials blew up a beached whale and showered the beach with blubber.
V6CLumsir34.why: Cited as the direct link to the infamous exploding whale footage, and used for jokes about explosions and whales.

V9jlo4Ht2YA.summary: A sketch from the Seattle comedy show Almost Live! in which Pat Cashman plays a US Bell rep explaining the new 425 area code. It first aired in 1997.
V9jlo4Ht2YA.why: Seattle-area commenters bring it up as a nostalgic local joke when area codes or Eastside versus Seattle rivalry come up.

VADudzQGvU8.summary: Perry Metzger, an Emacs user since 1983, gives a talk on why he has used one editor for decades. It mixes history, philosophy and speculation about Emacs's future, and teaches some Emacs fundamentals.
VADudzQGvU8.why: Mentioned in Emacs threads as a talk on long-term editor commitment and on Emacs's blocking limitations.

VAFd4FdbJxs.summary: A one-minute George Carlin clip on conspiracies, making the point that powerful people with shared interests need no formal conspiracy.
VAFd4FdbJxs.why: Quoted to argue that aligned elites act in concert without explicit collusion.

VBUUx0jUKxc.summary: Graphic body-camera footage of the January 2016 fatal shooting of Daniel Shaver by an Arizona police officer in a hotel hallway, released after the officer's acquittal.
VBUUx0jUKxc.why: HN links it as stark evidence in discussions of police accountability and use of force, with a warning about its content.

VD1cP8SK3Q0.summary: A 2018 VICE News Tonight interview with Apple CEO Tim Cook, in which he discusses privacy as a core company value, the Facebook breach, and Apple's iCloud arrangement in China.
VD1cP8SK3Q0.why: Commenters cite it as a primary source for Cook's own words on Apple's privacy stance and on how iCloud data is handled in China.

VFkyV7d5t8o.summary: A scene from the film Disclosure showing its virtual reality interface, including a 3D file system visualizer.
VFkyV7d5t8o.why: Referenced as the memorable movie origin of the 3D file system browser and early VR depictions.

VKHFZBUTA4k.summary: A classic 1967 comedy sketch from At Last the 1948 Show, with Tim Brooke-Taylor, John Cleese, Graham Chapman and Marty Feldman as four prosperous Yorkshiremen trying to outdo each other with exaggerated tales of childhood poverty. It is the precursor to the version later performed by Monty Python.
VKHFZBUTA4k.why: Commenters post it as a joke whenever a thread turns to one-upping hardship or nostalgic reminiscing.

VMqcLUqYqrs.summary: A short clip, apparently the opening scene of the TV series The Newsroom, in which a character answers why America is not the greatest country in the world. It is a brief political monologue.
VMqcLUqYqrs.why: Cited as a quick reference to that Newsroom monologue when a thread touches on American decline.

VQPIdZvoV4g.summary: The 'Machine that goes PING!' sketch from Monty Python's The Meaning of Life, in which hospital staff fuss over a machine while ignoring the patient.
VQPIdZvoV4g.why: Posted as a joke in threads about monitoring, observability and alarms.

VTSCppeFzX4.summary: A six-minute sketch from That Mitchell and Webb Look in which a speaker argues you should never drink more than slightly less than two drinks, the mildly intoxicated sweet spot before drunken madness.
VTSCppeFzX4.why: HN uses it as a joke reference in threads about alcohol, cannabis and the Ballmer Peak, not as a recommendation.

VUoXtddNPAM.summary: The full Malvina Reynolds recording of the folk song 'Little Boxes', a satire of identical suburban tract housing, later popularized as the Weeds theme. The upload includes the lyrics.
VUoXtddNPAM.why: Mostly cited as a joke or passing reference when conversation touches on conformity or identical houses.

VVJSjeHDvfY.summary: A Tesla Model S/X owner films his drive on US-101 in the lane where a fatal Model X Autopilot crash occurred, showing the car steering toward the lane divider without any warning.
VVJSjeHDvfY.why: It is cited as evidence that other drivers could reproduce the Autopilot behavior in the fatal crash, mostly in critical discussions of Autopilot safety.

VVJldn_MmMY.summary: C-SPAN footage of the L0pht hacker collective testifying before the US Senate Governmental Affairs Committee on May 19, 1998. The members discuss internet and computer security weaknesses. The uploader says the media remembered only the claim that they could take down the internet in 30 minutes.
VVJldn_MmMY.why: Cited as a historical reference when HN discusses L0pht, Mudge or Joe Grand, rather than recommended as a watch.

VWDFgzAjr1k.summary: Not Just Bikes visits the Toronto Islands, home to Canada's only car-free neighbourhood. He explains the waiting list and strict ownership rules and asks why more such places aren't built.
VWDFgzAjr1k.why: Used as a concrete example of what a car-free neighbourhood looks like and of the demand for them.

VfUgT2YoPzI.summary: A short clip of a TiVo paid-programming broadcast from the early 2000s, which TiVo used to send guide data and service updates to DVRs over cable TV before broadband was common.
VfUgT2YoPzI.why: Commenters cite it as a concrete example of distributing data over TV broadcasts in discussions of unusual data channels.

VfjjiHGuHoc.summary: Danny MacAskill tries to destroy carbon fiber bike wheels by riding trials tricks through downtown Glasgow, including on bare rims on concrete.
VfjjiHGuHoc.why: Used as evidence that carbon wheels and rims are far tougher than their fragile reputation suggests.

Vhh_GeBPOhs.summary: A short clip of Steve Ballmer at a Microsoft event chanting "developers" over and over. It became a lasting internet meme.
Vhh_GeBPOhs.why: Posted purely as a joke whenever the word "developers" comes up in a thread about Microsoft or software.

VjzqO6UOPFQ.summary: A clip from The Wire (season 4, episode 7) in which a former mayor tells Tommy Carcetti about having to "eat shit" from each constituency during his term. It is a parable about the unpleasant compromises of political leadership.
VjzqO6UOPFQ.why: Cited as a parable that leaders must absorb criticism and do the unpleasant work nobody else will.

Vk5bxHetL4s.summary: PBS Space Time explains how general relativity permits warp drive in principle and covers recent theoretical advances toward solving the negative energy problem.
Vk5bxHetL4s.why: Linked as a readable summary of where warp drive theory stands when threads discuss recent papers.

VkVs4ZqWgN8.summary: A one-minute clip of Steve Jobs describing how he cut Apple's product line down to a four-quadrant matrix of consumer and pro, desktop and portable, during the 1997 turnaround.
VkVs4ZqWgN8.why: Cited in Apple product-line threads as a reminder of the focus Jobs brought by reducing offerings to a few great products.

VogqOscJYvk.summary: Olivier Giroux's CppCon 2019 talk recounts the roughly ten-year effort to bring std::atomic and the C++ memory model to CUDA GPUs, through ten stories from that work.
VogqOscJYvk.why: Cited as a reference when discussing NVIDIA's C++ memory model, libcu++, and GPU C++ resources.

VpEpAFGplnI.summary: A short demo of real-time sparse voxel octree rendering, shown by Jon Olick at Siggraph 2008. It shows a detailed model rendered by ray casting through the octree.
VpEpAFGplnI.why: Cited in discussions of voxel rendering, id Software's research and Euclideon-style claims as an early demonstration of the technique.

Vpdt7omPoa0.summary: An Associated Press clip from the 2016 Nevada Republican caucuses in which Donald Trump says he loves the poorly educated.
Vpdt7omPoa0.why: Mostly quoted critically in political arguments about voters and leaders, not recommended for any content.

Vpwkdmwui3k.summary: A Washington Post clip of President Trump and NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg in a tense exchange at the July 2018 NATO summit, where Trump criticized Germany's reliance on Russian energy.
Vpwkdmwui3k.why: HN cites it as evidence in arguments about European dependence on Russian gas and NATO spending, especially after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

VreG1iC65Lc.summary: Footage of the Mercedes A-Class production line at the Rastatt plant in Germany, filmed in 2013. It shows robots and fixtures working through assembly.
VreG1iC65Lc.why: Used as a concrete example of modern car assembly, with short cycle times and heavy robotic automation, in manufacturing and automation threads.

Vrxyr1CjiSM.summary: A two-minute clip of the self-driving cars from the film Minority Report, showing driverless vehicles with rotating passenger compartments on a highway.
Vrxyr1CjiSM.why: HN refers to it as a pop-culture picture of autonomous vehicles, not as something to watch for its content.

VtvjbmoDx-I.summary: The famous 1984 Super Bowl commercial introducing the Apple Macintosh, directed by Ridley Scott and based on Orwell's novel.
VtvjbmoDx-I.why: HN mostly references it as a cultural touchstone, either praised as one of the most powerful ads ever or used ironically to criticize Apple's later behavior.

VuDSz06BT2g.summary: Out of Spec Reviews takes a one-hour drive in an Avatr 11 running Huawei's Qiankun ADS 3.2 driver assistance system in China, billed as the best FSD-like system there.
VuDSz06BT2g.why: HN cites it as a real-world look at Huawei's lidar-based driver assistance when comparing against Tesla FSD.

VuqZ8AqmLPY.summary: A short Apple Get a Mac ad that mocks Windows Vista's constant security pop-up prompts.
VuqZ8AqmLPY.why: Cited, often ironically, in macOS security threads as Apple's mockery of permission prompts that macOS later adopted itself.

Vxq9yj2pVWk.summary: A two-minute compilation of TV and film scenes where investigators say 'enhance' and a blurry image becomes sharp. It mocks the trope.
Vxq9yj2pVWk.why: Used as a joke or critique whenever someone expects impossible image upscaling or recovery of detail.

VzFpg271sm8.summary: World Builder is a short film by Bruce Branit in which a man uses holographic tools to build a world for the woman he loves.
VzFpg271sm8.why: Cited as a sci-fi vision of editing a world in VR, and a reference point for how VR and world-building tools have caught up.
